pages.title: Cuisine Table
pages.text: Three slots: the bottom-left takes $(thing)ingredients$(), the top-left takes a $(thing)tool$(), and the right side gives the product.$(br2)Taking the product consumes one portion of ingredients and costs the tool 1 durability; a tool that runs out breaks.$(br2)Only $(thing)one player$() can use it at a time — anyone else is told it is occupied — and the product slot is emptied when the interface is closed.

pages.title: How It Differs From a Cutting Board
pages.text: Like the $(thing)stonecutter$(), it resolves the $(thing)recipe conflicts$() you get when $(thing)one input has several outputs$(), while a cutting board only allows one output per input.
